records.name: Ester
records.evidence_locations: Rajandi PDF56–57/printed58–59, Esther entry (text layer; the column break after “Eston” is not used).
records.facts_used: Ester comes from the biblical Esther. Her name is linked to the Babylonian love goddess Ishtar and to a word for ‘star’, the evening and morning star, figuratively ‘good fortune’. records.name: Urban
records.evidence_locations: Rajandi PDF168/printed170 (text layer); Mägiste 1929 PDF56 “Urban -i (KA Vrban ~ Vrbann, Wd. Urban)”, KA = central archive wackenbooks (key PDF15).
records.facts_used: Urban comes from the Latin name Urbanus, ‘townsman’; in antiquity it meant a Roman, since urbs, ‘the city’, was Rome. Estonian forms include Urban, Urbanus, Urbo, Urbas and Urbus. Urbanus day used to be marked in Estonia on 25 May. The old Roman name also survives in Estonian surnames such as Urban, Urbanik and Urbus, and appears in the parish wackenbooks of the 16th and 17th centuries as Vrban.
